independent_audit_fixes_round3.source: independent audit of the committed code (5 confirmed findings for concept-06: 2 major, 3 minor)
independent_audit_fixes_round3.method: Every figure below is a peak-ink measurement taken from a freshly regenerated PNG decoded with a pure-python PNG reader: the darkest/brightest pixel inside the text rect against that rect's modal background, WCAG relative-luminance ratio. 'modal' is the most common non-ground colour in the same rect - when modal == peak the glyphs reach their declared token exactly. Shots were taken over file:// CDP at 1280x900 and 760x900 with webfonts blocked, exactly as the audit's own shots were, so the numbers are directly comparable to the finding text. Temp shots deleted after inspection.

fixes.finding: A3-1 (major, contrast): in both friendly themes the 10px meta tier (--fs-2xs on --text-muted) rendered below the 4.5:1 small-text floor across the rail counts, eyebrow, destination tallies, index breadcrumbs and copy step nav; the same roles in glass/basic/retro reached their declared token exactly.
fixes.root_cause: Size and weight, not hue. The friendly faces are the only ones whose --body-font resolves to an installed 'Quicksand' (the others fall through to the system face); Quicksand's thin geometric stems never reach full pixel coverage at 10px/400. The token itself passes (friendly-light #5F5866 = 6.41:1, friendly-dark #9E98A8 = 5.88:1).
fixes.change: concept CSS: the tier is now two custom properties on .c06 -- --c06-fs-meta (default var(--fs-2xs)) and --c06-fw-meta (default 400) -- --c06-fs-meta replaces var(--fs-2xs) in all 21 tier rules, and --c06-fw-meta is carried by 21 declarations (the 19 tier rules that declared no weight of their own, .c06-rail-count whose explicit 400 became the variable, and the 'Recommended' chip); .c06-table th keeps its own 600. [data-theme="friendly-dark"] .c06, [data-theme="friendly-light"] .c06 raise them to 11.5px / 600. 11.5px sits between --fs-xs (11px) and --fs-sm (12px) so the tier still reads a full step under the 12px description line. Size alone was measured to be insufficient (the rail count '95' peaks at 4.28:1 at 11.5px/400 and only 4.85:1 at 13px, which would already be louder than the description); Quicksand 600 resolves to its Bold face. .c06-rail-link takes the matching 600 step in the friendly faces only (:not([aria-current]) so the current item keeps its 700), so the label still leads its own count on size.

fix_notes_2026_08_21_scroll_integrity.scope: concept-06-directory-take-2.js only (one function, buildFrame). No CSS change was needed, no HTML, no _shared/_shared2 module, no other concept, no tooling, no hub/index.

finding_fixed_here.finding: [major] stale-virtualizer-window - the All Settings index kept the row window it had computed for a SHORTER scroller whenever the scroller grew without a width change, leaving a blank strip of empty sheet below the last painted row.
finding_fixed_here.detected_by: tools/harness/run-suite.js scroll, cases all-resize-stale-window and all-stress-resize-stale-window (negative-control proven). Repro: scroll to 20,000px at 1280x560, then resize to 1280x1200 - height only, so no narrow/wide flip re-renders the surface.
finding_fixed_here.root_cause: drawIndex() sizes the window from els.scroll.scrollTop AND els.scroll.clientHeight, but the only live trigger was the scroller's 'scroll' event (onIndexScroll). The one ResizeObserver the concept already had watched #pmStage and called syncNarrow(), which acts on WIDTH alone and re-renders nothing when only the height moves. So a pure height change (window resize, the chat dock closing) produced no repaint: the page received the resize events, the scroller grew, and the row window stayed sized for the old, shorter band. The width leg of the same trap MASKED this - crossing the 880px narrow breakpoint re-renders the surface and repaints the window as a side effect - which is why only the height-only leg failed.
finding_fixed_here.fix: buildFrame() now attaches a second ResizeObserver, to #c06Scroll itself, which calls drawIndex(true) whenever the scroller's own clientHeight actually changes and the current view is the index (ui.view.kind === 'all'), coalesced through one requestAnimationFrame. drawIndex() has no start-index/count short-circuit - it recomputes start and end from the CURRENT scrollTop and clientHeight on every call - so the repaint really does resize the window rather than reuse the old count. The existing stage observer is untouched; the width path still runs through syncNarrow().
finding_fixed_here.no_feedback_loop: The observed box is the scroller, not its content. #c06Scroll is flex-sized (flex: 1 1 auto, min-height: 0) inside .c06-main, so the spacer divs drawIndex writes inside it cannot feed back into its height. The clientHeight equality guard is a second, independent stop, and the ui.view.kind gate keeps the observer inert on every non-index route.
finding_fixed_here.measured_before: scroll suite, height-only leg (deep scroll at 1280x560 then grow to 1280x1200), after 4 real resize events seen by the page: #/all rowsPainted 20, rowBandCoverage 0.76, blank bottom strip 261px, point coverage 15/18; #/all?stress=1 rowsPainted 20, rowBandCoverage 0.79, blank bottom strip 232px, point coverage 15/18. Both cases FAIL.
